name: FlowEval
description: Despite recent progress in open-domain dialogue evaluation, how to develop automatic metrics remains an open problem. We explore the potential of dialogue evaluation featuring dialog act information, which was hardly explicitly modeled in previous methods. However, defined at the utterance level in general, dialog act is of coarse granularity, as an utterance can contain multiple segments possessing different functions. Hence, we propose segment act, an extension of dialog act from utterance level to segment level, and crowdsource a large-scale dataset for it. To utilize segment act flows, sequences of segment acts, for evaluation, we develop the first consensus-based dialogue evaluation framework, FlowEval. This framework provides a reference-free approach for dialog evaluation by finding pseudo-references. reputation: A specialized dialogue-evaluation benchmark that is cited in work on segment-level dialogue acts and reference-free evaluation, but it is not a mainstream general-purpose benchmark.
notes: Primarily used to evaluate automatic dialogue metrics rather than end-task generation; results are often reported as correlation with human judgments and are not directly comparable across datasets.
